questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
Building a hospital has a social cost of $200 million. The social benefit is $240 million; external benefit is $150 million. What can be concluded from this information?

options.A: external benefit is greater than external cost
options.B: external benefit is greater than private benefit
options.C: private benefit is greater than private cost
options.D: the project should not take place

options.A: marginal expenditure

options.C: total expenditure
options.D: total utility

questions.questionText: What is a characteristic of a highly contestable industry?

options.A: a reduction in abnormal profits
options.B: a substantial volume of advertising by existing firms
options.C: relatively few firms in the industry
options.D: significant sunk costs incurred by new entrants to the industry

questions.questionText: The diagram shows cost and revenue curves for a firm. MC cost, revenue AC P P P

The list provides characteristics of the market in which firm X operates. ● Firms in the market spend a lot of money on advertising. ● Firms in the market experience a high level of uncertainty. ● Start-up costs for new firms entering the market are relatively high. ● The largest five firms in the market control 85% of total sales. In which market structure is firm X operating?

options.A: monopoly
options.B: monopolistic competition
options.C: oligopoly
options.D: perfect competition

questions.questionText: Which statement about the ‘kinked demand curve’ model of oligopoly is incorrect?

options.A: The kink in the demand curve of each firm is based on expectations about other firms’ responses to changes in its price.
options.B: The marginal revenue curve of the firm has a vertical segment at the market price.
options.C: The model explains how the equilibrium market price is determined.
options.D: The model suggests price stickiness within a certain range of marginal costs.

questions.questionText: As firm X grows in size, it specialises in a narrower range of products. Which economies of scale will the firm be less able to benefit from?

options.A: financial
options.B: marketing
options.C: risk-bearing
options.D: technical

questions.questionText: What would economists agree should be the aim of any healthcare system?

options.A: to meet all the healthcare demands of the population
options.B: to provide every patient with the latest and best available treatment
options.C: to provide free medical treatment
options.D: to secure the maximum health gain from the resources available

questions.questionText: A producer of a good causes pollution. When will a specific tax on the production of the good be most effective in reducing output?

options.A: when there is price elastic demand and price elastic supply
options.B: when there is price elastic demand and price inelastic supply
options.C: when there is price inelastic demand and price elastic supply
options.D: when there is price inelastic demand and price inelastic supply

questions.questionText: Governments often aim to reduce income inequalities. The diagram shows the effects of using taxation and benefits to try to achieve this aim. 100 000 average income per household 80 000 key ($ per year) original income 60 000 disposable income final income 40 000
000 bottom 2nd 3rd 4th top 20% 20% 20% 20% 20% household income What can be concluded about the effects of taxes and benefits from the diagram?

options.A: All income groups are better off except those earning more than 40000 dollars per year.
options.B: Benefits paid to the lower income groups are not a burden because they are not paid out of tax revenues.
options.C: The average final income of the top 20% exceeds the combined final incomes of the other groups.
options.D: The progressive taxation system still favours the top 20% over the bottom 20% of households.

questions.questionText: Which government policy would not be classified as regulation?

options.A: bans on heroin and cocaine consumption
options.B: compulsory wearing of seatbelts in cars and coaches
options.C: licences for the extraction of water from lakes and rivers
options.D: taxation of cigarettes and tobacco products

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the initial position of a labour market. weekly S wage D O number of workers The government increases the number of statutory paid holidays to which workers are entitled from 10 days a year to 15 days a year. How will this affect the supply and demand curves in the diagram? employers’ workers’ demand curve supply curve

options.A: shifts to left shifts to right
options.B: shifts to left shifts to left
options.C: shifts to right shifts to right
options.D: shifts to right shifts to left

questions.questionText: The diagram represents the demand and supply of labour in a competitive industry. S wage W D O L labour What is true about unit of labour L when they are paid wage W?

options.A: L is paid only economic rent.
options.B: L is paid an element of economic rent and transfer earnings.
options.C: L is paid below transfer earnings and leaves the industry.
options.D: L is paid exactly transfer earnings and remains in work.

questions.questionText: Which combination of characteristics is usually associated with a developing country?

options.A: high death rate and low levels of productivity
options.B: high gross domestic product and low infant mortality
options.C: low birth rate and a large proportion of income from primary industries
options.D: low exports of capital and a large tertiary sector

questions.questionText: What is the best description of sustainable economic development?

options.A: a long term increase in the actual output of an economy
options.B: a long term increase in the living standards without damage to the environment
options.C: a long term increase in the productive potential of an economy
options.D: a long term increase in the living standards of every member of society

questions.questionText: Which change in the labour market could cause inflation if the government adopted an expansionary fiscal policy?

options.A: a decrease in the economy’s national minimum wage
options.B: a decrease in the power of the economy’s trade unions
options.C: an increase in the level of benefits paid to unemployed workers
options.D: an increase in the migration of workers into the country from overseas

questions.questionText: Which assumption is not made in the Keynesian model of national income and employment determination?

options.A: An increase in aggregate demand can increase real national income.
options.B: Interest rates move to equalise planned savings and investment.
options.C: Investment depends on the expectation of entrepreneurs.
options.D: Planned consumption is a function of national income.

questions.questionText: An economist once said “if you pay people not to work and tax them when they do, don’t be surprised if you get unemployment”. What is this an example of?

options.A: cyclical unemployment
options.B: frictional unemployment
options.C: structural unemployment
options.D: voluntary unemployment

questions.questionText: The table provides data for the external debt as a percentage of Gross National Income (GNI) for four countries in 2010 and 2015. external debt as % of GNI 2010 2015 Bulgaria 104.2 79.9 Georgia 85.6 109.4 India 17.2 23.4 Serbia 85.4 88.8 What can be deduced from the table?

options.A: All countries borrowed more money externally in 2015 than in 2010.
options.B: External borrowing grew more slowly than GNI in India.
options.C: Georgia borrowed the most money externally in 2015.
options.D: The burden of external debt changed least in Serbia.

questions.questionText: The following statistics are for Pakistan and refer to 2016. % GDP growth 5.7 population growth 2.0 rate of inflation 3.8 What was the approximate rate of growth of real GDP per capita for Pakistan in 2016?
In a 4-sector economy, consisting of households, firms, government and foreign trade, the level of national income is in equilibrium where

options.C: + I + G + (X – M) = Y. What must Y include for an equilibrium to exist?
options.A: C + S + M B C + S + T C S + T D S + T + M

questions.questionText: According to Keynesian theory, what will cause the rate of interest to rise?

options.A: a decrease in liquidity preference
options.B: a decrease in the level of national income
options.C: a decrease in the rate of investment
options.D: a decrease in the supply of money

questions.questionText: A government finances its public sector borrowing by selling securities to the non-bank private sector. What will follow?

options.A: The budget deficit will fall.
options.B: The deficit on the current account will increase.
options.C: The money supply will rise.
options.D: The national debt will increase.

questions.questionText: When would a central bank be able to exert the closest control over the money supply of the country?

options.A: If it intervened in the foreign exchange market to influence the value of domestic currency.
options.B: If it only issued domestic currency at a fixed price in exchange for US$.
options.C: If the country was part of a monetary union with other countries.
options.D: If the domestic currency was allowed to float freely in the foreign exchange market.

questions.questionText: A fall in domestic investment leads to an increase in unemployment. Which other problem might also be observed at the same time?

options.A: an increase in interest rates on loans for house purchase
options.B: an increase in the current account balance of payments deficit
options.C: an increase in the government budget deficit
